draft.title: Types of non-infectious disease
card: A non-infectious disease is not caused by a pathogen, so it cannot spread from one person to another. Its causes include genes, the environment, nutrition and how cells grow.
Genetic
caused by a faulty gene passed on from parents. Cystic fibrosis is an example.
Environmental
caused by exposure to something around us. Skin cancer can follow too much ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun.
Nutritional
caused by too little or too much of a nutrient. Scurvy comes from a lack of vitamin C.
draft.remember: Non-infectious diseases do not spread between people, and they can have genetic, environmental or nutritional causes.

a.q: A sailor on a long voyage with no fresh fruit develops scurvy. Which type of cause is this?
opts: Nutritional, from too little vitamin C
Genetic, from a faulty inherited gene
Infectious, from a pathogen on the ship
Environmental, from too much UV radiation
a.why: Scurvy comes from a lack of vitamin C in the diet, so its cause is nutritional. It is not infectious, because no pathogen is involved and it cannot spread to other sailors.
a.clue: Think about what the sailor was missing from the diet.

b.q: Priya has a skin cancer removed after years of outdoor work in Queensland. Why is her disease called non-infectious?
opts: It is not caused by a pathogen and cannot spread to others
It is caused by a faulty gene passed on from her parents
It has an environmental cause, so it cannot be infectious
It affects only one part of her body, so it cannot spread
b.why: A non-infectious disease is not caused by a pathogen, so other people cannot catch it from Priya. The environment is a cause here, but the reason it is non-infectious is the lack of a pathogen. Genes are not the only cause of non-infectious disease.
b.clue: Ask what it would take for someone else to catch it.

a.best: Nutritional, from too little vitamin C

b.best: It is not caused by a pathogen and cannot spread to others

problems.detail: The genetic bullet defines a genetic disease as 'caused by a faulty gene passed on from parents'. Genetic disorders can also come from new mutations or chromosome changes that are not inherited, such as most cases of Down syndrome. Year 12 students study mutation in Module 6, so this narrow definition can mislead them.

The card's first bullet and the chapter point list four kinds of cause: genes, environment, nutrition and how cells grow. The remember line lists only genetic, environmental and nutritional, so it drops cell growth (for example cancer) and sorts the causes differently from the card.
The first bullet names 'how cells grow' as a cause but gives no bullet or example for it. Students meet the category without learning what it means.

proposal.title: Types of non-infectious disease
card: A non-infectious disease is not caused by a pathogen, so it cannot spread from person to person. Its causes include genes, the environment, nutrition and how cells grow.
Genetic
caused by a change to a gene or chromosome. It may be inherited, as in cystic fibrosis, or come from a new mutation that neither parent had.
Environment and diet
caused by things around us or in our food. Smoking raises the risk of heart disease, and too little vitamin C causes scurvy.
Cell growth
caused by cells dividing out of control and forming a tumour, as in cancer. Ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun can trigger skin cancer.
proposal.remember: No pathogen means no spread. The causes are genes, surroundings, diet and uncontrolled cell growth.

a.q: A sailor on a long voyage with no fresh fruit develops scurvy. What is the cause?
opts: Too little of a nutrient in the diet
A changed gene passed on by a parent
A pathogen picked up on the ship
Cells in the body dividing out of control
a.why: Scurvy comes from a lack of vitamin C, a nutrient found in fresh fruit, so the cause is in the diet. It is not caused by a pathogen, so the other sailors cannot catch it from him.
a.clue: Think about what was missing from the sailor's meals.

b.q: Priya develops skin cancer after years of outdoor work in Queensland. What best explains her disease?
opts: UV triggered her skin cells to divide out of control
A pathogen she caught outdoors made her skin cells grow
Her cells grew out of control, so others can catch it
She lacked vitamin C, so her skin cells grew too fast
b.why: Cancer is cells dividing out of control, and UV from the sun can trigger it in skin. Uncontrolled cell growth is right, but no pathogen is involved, so her coworkers cannot catch it from her.
b.clue: Link the sun to what her cells did, then ask if it can spread.
